lines.en: Guided by the judge, I headed toward the Underworld's exit.
I was wearing a special blindfold, so I couldn't tell exactly where I was. It felt as though we were going up, but also as though we were going down.
In any case, only after we had walked for quite some time did the judge remove my blindfold.
[Follow this path.]
When I opened my eyes, I saw a narrow, dark side path.
This was probably the exit that led out of the Underworld without going through Charon, the ferryman.
[You would do well to find ‘ahead.’]
“What does that mean?”
When I looked back, the judge was already gone.

With no other choice, I walked along the side path. Soon, the light around me faded, and complete darkness settled in. At first, I could tell which way I was going by feeling along the wall, but before long, even that wall disappeared.
With nothing left to rely on, I felt like a ship adrift on a boundless sea without a buoy in sight.
The myth of Orpheus suddenly came to mind.
What would happen to me if I looked back here?
That was when faint, luminous writing appeared in the darkness.
[You're afraid of what's behind you. That poor child was, too.]
It was a message from Persephone.
[But remember this. To find ‘ahead,’ you must know where ‘behind’ is. After all, ‘ahead’ can only exist when there is a ‘behind.’]
Come to think of it, the judge had said something similar.
But hearing something that sounded profound wasn't enough to make me suddenly attain enlightenment and undergo some tremendous change.
[It seems you need a little motivation······.]
The strings of luminous letters hanging in the air stretched out, as though hesitating.
[Very well. She's already at the entrance to the labyrinth that crosses worldlines, so I cannot bring her here right away, but I can manage this much.]
Just as I wondered—could it be?
The strings of letters vanished all at once, and something small and faint, like a firefly, appeared before my eyes.
A distant light.
A very fragile, gentle light.
No one told me, but I knew what that light was.
It was Shin Yoosung from the 41st round.
I could tell from her voice alone.
How long she had been waiting.

If she was already at the threshold of crossing worldlines, time there would work differently from here. From my perspective, it hadn't been long since I sent Shin Yoosung off, but for her, years might already have passed.
The little light trembled again and again, then hesitated over something before cautiously speaking.
―Ajusshi.
She seemed to have been influenced by the young Shin Yoosung's memories.
―······I-I can call you that too, right? No··· may I?
A form of address was a bond. A desire to be tied to something. Perhaps that word, ‘ajusshi,’ was the last lingering attachment of Shin Yoosung from the 41st round. I smiled faintly and spoke.
“You're older than me now. Are you sure that's okay?”
The gentle light quivered once more.
As though playing, the light lightly touched my cheek, then drew away.
That simple warmth, that gesture······.
My heart hurt as though it were being torn apart.
She must have waited a long time.
And yet this child would have to wait longer.
“I'm sorry. I can't save you right away.”
The little light bobbed gently up and down, as though she understood.
―Don't push yourself. My story is already······.
“It isn't over.”
I spoke without giving her a chance to continue.
“After suffering for so many years, you can't let it end like this.”
“I'll never let that happen.”
The light looked at me and spoke.
With a plaintive tremor, as though confused.
―I came to know you through the memories of this world, ajusshi. But you······ why are you so good to me? You don't really know me, do you?
I didn't answer.
We had come to know each other through different mediums.
Just as Shin Yoosung from the 41st round had come to know me through her younger self's memories, I knew her through ‘Ways of Survival.’ And yet I couldn't properly explain that to her.
―It feels strange. I know I don't really know you, ajusshi, but when I'm with you, I feel completely understood. As though I'm standing before a ‘god’······.
If I really were a god, I'd be the most incompetent god in the world.
The feeling of being the world's most powerless god, knowing everything but unable to explain anything.
Shin Yoosung's light was rapidly fading.
Though I couldn't see her, I felt as though I knew what expression she was wearing.
―······Save me, ······please.
“I will.”
The tail of light wavering in the air grew smaller and smaller, and I reached out to touch it.
It felt as though my heart was being squeezed.
Shin Yoosung's despair. That long wait······.
An indescribable sorrow cut through my heart like a knife.
Little by little, I began to understand Persephone's words. That only with a ‘behind’ could I move ‘ahead.’
This was my ‘behind,’ and at the same time, the ‘ahead’ I had to move toward.
Perhaps Yoo Joonghyuk had felt this way, too. He kept returning to the past, yet could move forward only by returning.
The moment I became certain of my direction, my surroundings slowly began to distort.
Strings of luminous letters appeared over the dispersing darkness.
[I've held her back for a little while with my power, but if you want to save her, you have almost no time left.]
I remembered the faint warmth of Shin Yoosung that lingered in my hand.
Persephone spoke.
[Remember. A human being is a ‘story.’ So when you recover her, no one knows how much of her story will remain.]
With those final words, I was sucked away somewhere.
Aaaaah.
The wails of the spirits receded, and the vivid sensations of my body returned one by one.
Bright sunlight pierced my eyelids.
Feeling how damp my back had become, I opened my eyes with a start and saw a familiar face.
“······Ajusshi?”
The young Shin Yoosung was looking at me. The child's clear eyes. Those eyes gave me certainty. My pounding heart gradually settled.
I was back.
As I slowly caught my breath, the muscles throughout my body began working properly again.
[Hidden Scenario ― ‘Queen of the Underworld’ has ended.]
[You have received 15000 coins as a hidden scenario reward.]
The reward for the updated scenario had come in, too.
It seemed the rookie dokkaebi had handled things properly.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ congratulates you on your safe return.]
As I read the incoming indirect message, a belated surge of anger rose in me.
If that bastard Dionysus hadn't thrown me into Tartarus, I wouldn't have had to go through all that. I'd nearly ended up trapped in Tartarus with Kim Namwoon, spending my life building Gunpla.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ requests reconciliation with you.]
[You have received 7942 coins in sponsorship.]
What was this, a pager-generation apology?
Still, since he'd given me coins, I'd let him off this once.
[1 new hidden scenario has arrived.]
I immediately checked the newly arrived hidden scenario.
<Hidden Scenario ― Snake Hunt>
Category : Hidden
Difficulty : S-
Clear Conditions : Hunt the target in the sixth main scenario area.
Time Limit : Until the main scenario ends
Reward : 80000 coins, the confidence of the ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring.’
Failure : Entry to the Underworld prohibited
As expected, Persephone's task had arrived in the form of a hidden scenario.
[A scenario alert will activate automatically when the target appears nearby.]
Snake Hunt.
The scenario didn't specify the target, but if it was a ‘snake’ that would appear in the next scenario, I had a rough idea which one it was.
As I slowly sat up, Shin Yoosung asked worriedly.
“Ajusshi, are you all right now?”
“Yeah. I'm fine.”
“Sangah-unnie told me to keep a close eye on you······.”
Come to think of it, I'd asked Yoo Sangah to take care of things right before I collapsed.
“Where's Yoo Sangah-ssi?”

Yoo Sangah wasn't hard to find. She was asleep nearby, curled up on the bare ground. Looking at her sleeping face, I couldn't help recalling the sight of Persephone transformed into Yoo Sangah, and my face grew hot.
Still, a cheongsam and a garter belt······ that really had been something.
“Unnie was awake until just a little while ago. She only just fell asleep.”
“Ah.”
“She also told me to make sure I let the others know if you still didn't wake up.”
Her next words landed a critical hit of guilt.
There were pitch-black circles under Yoo Sangah's eyes. She must have been struggling with her own hangover, too······.
A cheongsam? A garter belt?
Damn it, I was trash.
“You're finally awake?”
Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung were approaching from some distance away.
Judging by how sweaty they were, it seemed the two had just returned from a morning sparring session somewhere.
Jung Heewon spoke.
“Now that you're awake, Dokja-ssi, we'd better get ready to leave, too.”
“Get ready to leave?”
“Everyone else has already left.”
Come to think of it, the people who had been gathered all around us yesterday were gone.
I asked.
“What happened overnight?”
“The notice for the sixth main scenario appeared.”
······Already?
Before I could ask, a huge string of letters appeared in the sky.
[Survivors, please gather at Yongsan Station.]
We immediately packed our belongings and set off.
Since we were already in Yongsan District, getting to the station wasn't particularly difficult. I carried Yoo Sangah on my back, while Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung took the rest of the luggage.
Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung followed us, keeping well apart from each other.
Yoo Joonghyuk's group was nowhere to be seen.
When we reached the area around the station a little later, it was already teeming with survivors.
It was hard to believe so many people were still alive in Seoul. They were all looking at a giant screen suspended in the air.
“Is that the place?”
My companions and I looked up at the screen together.
It showed the same scene I'd seen in the Underworld.
A forest covered in dense jungle.
And monsters running through that forest.
Up close, they would certainly have been frightening monsters, but with the entire landscape in view, they looked like nothing more than part of a vast ecosystem.
I could see incarnations, too.
Some people who had already begun hunting were holding up severed monster heads and grinning our way. Those dokkaebi bastards. They'd edited it to look just like a travel advertisement.
Someone spoke.
“Huh? Wasn't that a Japanese guy just now?”
If I remembered correctly, the sixth scenario was a special event scenario shared with another dome.
The man who had just appeared on-screen was probably ‘Izumi,’ a famous Japanese incarnation.
The Tokyo Dome was progressing faster than us, so they must have entered the sixth scenario earlier, too.
In several respects, Korea was starting at a relative disadvantage.
[A new main scenario has arrived.]
The scenario details appeared along with the message.
<Main Scenario # 6 ― ????? >
Category : Main
Difficulty : ???
Clear Conditions : ???
Time Limit : ???
Reward : ???
Failure : ―
“Huh? There's no difficulty or clear conditions?”
“······What the hell are we supposed to do? It's all question marks!”
The bewildered people called up the window again and again, but the scenario details remained plastered with question marks.
Of course, I already knew, so I wasn't surprised.
Because this scenario······.
“Apparently, only a select number of people can undertake this scenario.”
A tall, middle-aged man stood where the voice had come from.
“It's been a while, Kim Dokja-nim. This is our first formal introduction.”
······So this man was here, too.
Just as I was about to speak, the man offered his hand first.
“I'm Jeon Ildo. I'm known as the ‘Neutral King.’”
“I'm Kim Dokja.”
Jeon Ildo, the Neutral King.
One of the few kings of Seoul who had survived the ‘Battle for the Absolute Throne,’ along with Cha Sangkyung, the Maitreya King, and Min Jiwon, the King of Beauty.
I also remembered something striking about Jeon Ildo.
During the ‘Battle for the Throne,’ he had been the only king to relinquish the throne of his own free will.

“Both during the Battle for the Throne and this time, I was deeply impressed by your accomplishments, Dokja-nim. You have no idea how much my sponsor goes on about you. Tells me to be even half as good as you.”
Jeon Ildo gave a friendly-looking smile.
Come to think of it, who was this man's sponsor again?
I immediately activated my skill.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
A summary list that included only his attributes and sponsor.
[Summary list settings have been changed.]
<Character Summary List>
Character : Jeon Ildo
Exclusive Attributes : Inept Intellectual (General), Neutral King (Hero)
Constellation Sponsor : Expert at Sitting on the Fence

······Now that I'd looked, I wondered why I'd bothered. Of course this constellation would be his sponsor. At first glance, ‘Expert at Sitting on the Fence’ might suggest a two-timing expert—some old-fashioned constellation entangled in complicated affairs—but it was actually the modifier of a ‘king.’
[A constellation advocating neutral diplomacy reveals its modifier.]
[The constellation ‘Expert at Sitting on the Fence’ expresses goodwill toward you.]
Expert at Sitting on the Fence was the modifier of ‘Gwanghaegun,’ a king of Joseon famous as a master of neutral diplomacy.
Jeon Ildo's attribute wasn't ‘Neutral King’ for nothing.
“I'd like to hear a little more about what you just said. What do you mean, only a ‘select number of people’ will undertake the scenario?”
“Ah, so you hadn't heard.”
As expected, the kings with their quick access to information seemed to know something.
Of course, when it came to knowing things, I probably knew the most, but I still needed to hear him out. Things might have changed from the ‘Ways of Survival’ I knew.
“According to the information the lower-grade dokkaebis disclosed this morning, they'll be selecting volunteers separately for this scenario.”
“Volunteers?”
“Yes. Not everyone has to participate in this scenario. And there's no penalty for not participating. Given the scenarios we've had so far, those are unbelievable terms.”
Just as I remembered.
I pointed at the screen and asked.
“The participants will be going there, then?”
“That's what I've heard.”
Perhaps they'd overheard Jeon Ildo, because relieved voices rose here and there.
“What? We don't all have to go?”
“Fuck, thank god. I pissed myself a little when I saw that monster······ why's it so damn big?”
By this point, the incarnations in the scenarios fell into three broad groups.
First, those who watched how things were going, then quietly slunk away.
Most of them belonged to no group. They were probably thinking they were safe now, that they could get by on other people's efforts.
But they were wrong.
At a certain point, the difficulty of every scenario in the Star Stream rose exponentially.
They would probably face a terrible future as the price of not participating in the scenario.
“······Looks like fun.”
Then there was the second group.
Those who had already adapted to some extent to the harsh conditions of the scenarios.
People who strengthened their resolve while watching the screen, or checked their equipment in advance.
They would probably survive ‘for the time being.’
And finally, the third group······.
“Jeon Ildo-nim! Where are you?”
Someone called for Jeon Ildo from outside the crowd.
Jeon Ildo looked at his watch and groaned.
“It's that time already.”
“Go ahead. I'll be fine.”
“No, I can't go alone. That would defeat the purpose.”
“······What do you mean?”
“Kim Dokja-nim, the truth is, I came here to escort you.”
“Me?”
Jeon Ildo nodded.
“A world without a king.”
After saying those words, he briefly looked around.
It lasted only a moment, but I felt countless people's gazes turn our way.
As though he'd noticed those gazes, Jeon Ildo continued with an inscrutable smile.
“The kings left in that unfortunate world are eagerly awaiting your arrival.”
The final, third group.
Those who used others to survive.
I followed Jeon Ildo to where the kings had gathered.
They were on Yongsan Station's central platform. Their meeting room was screened off by an enormous tent they'd obtained from who knew where.
Dozens of sentries guarded the tent. Every one of them looked formidable.
They seemed to be elite troops the kings had trained.
While we were fighting Shin Yoosung, they had probably been hunting the monsters running rampant in other areas.
“I'm sorry, but only ‘kings’ are allowed beyond this point.”
When the sentry stopped us, I turned to my companions.
Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung nodded, as though they already understood the situation.
I temporarily entrusted Yoo Sangah, whom I'd been carrying on my back, to Lee Hyunsung.
“Dokja-ssi. If anything happens, scream right away. Got it?”
Hearing Jung Heewon say that was truly reassuring.
I gave her a small smile, then threw open the tent flap.
[The Sound Wave Blocking skill is active in this area.]
Well, well. Even Sound Wave Blocking?
They seemed to have put together a reasonably convincing setup······.
Inside, a round table stood in a spacious area.
There were even a few pieces of jerky and some biscuits on the table, obtained from who knew where.
Their chairs were all different.
Some sat in plastic chairs, others in wooden ones, and one person had brought an entire sofa. But whatever they sat on, their seats were unmistakably thrones.
The surviving kings were there.

“That's why I said it would be better for our group to go! Korea is a latecomer. Do you think you can handle the ones who've already established themselves there? But it would be different if our group went. If I went······!”
The middle-aged man's booming voice died away as I entered.
Every king was looking at me.
“The last king has arrived.”
Min Jiwon, the King of Beauty, spoke.
I gave her a brief greeting and looked around at the kings.
Yoo Joonghyuk······ wasn't here. Well, that was only natural, wasn't it?
There were five kings in attendance, excluding me.
Min Jiwon, the King of Beauty.
Cha Sangkyung, the Maitreya King.
Jeon Ildo, the Neutral King.
The King of Wanderers.
That made four, and the remaining one······.
Strange.
I didn't know this person?
“Who are you?”
“I'm Kim Dokja.”
“Ah, you're······ ahem, hmm. I'm ‘Yoo Hyunho,’ the President of Yeouido.”
······The President of Yeouido?
The president should already be dead. What nonsense was this?
Min Jiwon added in a displeased voice.
“······Yoo Hyunho-ssi isn't a king, but he leads a faction, so he's been allowed to attend.”
“Kings, my foot! Do you all really think we're living in the Joseon era? We live in an age of liberal democracy. Get a grip, please!”
I immediately activated the summary version of [Character List].
<Character Summary List>
Character : Yoo Hyunho
Exclusive Attribute : Corrupt Politician (Rare)
Constellation Sponsor : Master of State Affairs Manipulation
Exclusive Skills : [Bribe Taking Lv.5], [Army Command Lv.4], [Corrupt Power Lv.6], [Control of the Masses Lv.7]······.
······Suddenly, I thought I might remember him.
A politician who had cleared the first scenario at the National Assembly building and survived.
There had definitely been someone like that in a few rounds.
Normally, they all died when Yeouido was wiped out during the monster flood, but it seemed he'd been lucky this time.
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ is enraged at the corrupt Joseon official.]
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ dislikes the incarnation ‘Yoo Hyunho.’]
I wondered what that was about, but it was probably because of Yoo Hyunho's sponsor.
Which Joseon official had been a master of manipulating state affairs again······?
A shame. If Yoo Sangah were here, I could have asked her.
“And ‘Lee Sookyung’-ssi here······ is attending for a similar reason. I don't know if you've heard of her, but she's known as the ‘King of Wanderers.’”
The King of Wanderers looked at me. She was still wearing a mask. I stared at it for a moment, then turned toward the others.
“That's enough introductions. I'd like to know why you called me here.”
In response, Jeon Ildo, who occupied the central seat at the table, spoke.
“We intend to select representatives here to participate in the ‘sixth scenario.’”
So that was their purpose, just as I'd thought.
Yoo Hyunho picked up where Jeon Ildo left off.

“The people gathered here currently lead the largest factions in the Seoul Dome. Your group is relatively small, Kim Dokja-ssi, but given your considerable contribution to the scenarios, we've specially invited you. You should consider it an honor.”
“Ah······ is that so?”
Specially? An honor?
What a joke.
This bastard had been hiding somewhere, waiting for an opportunity while I busted my ass clearing scenarios······.
What had he just said to me?
Yoo Hyunho looked around at everyone and spoke.
“As I've said, it's time we left barbarism behind. We briefly returned to primitive times and repeated the ‘war of all against all,’ but at heart, we are law-
abiding citizens who act according to the established social contract theory! So shouldn't we select the participants for the next scenario through a democratic process?”
It sounded like plain, pathetic bullshit, but mixing in some plausible words made it sound like fairly convincing bullshit. Min Jiwon answered.
“What democratic process are you referring to?”
“As I said earlier, I believe it's right to allocate participant slots according to the size of each faction.”
Jeon Ildo immediately objected.
“If we're simply going by numbers, I understand the Yeouido faction is the largest. That proposal isn't equitable.”

“Jeon Ildo-ssi, that's disappointing to hear. Aren't we all fellow Koreans, in the end? Whether more people from one particular faction get chosen isn't really important. Once we enter the scenario, we'll be facing other countries anyway. At that point, all this talk of who belongs to which group will vanish. Are we going to fight among ourselves with the enemy right in front of us?”
It was blatant political deflection, but Jeon Ildo wasn't such a pushover, either.
“If it doesn't matter who gets chosen, I don't see why we need to choose more people from your group.”
“Ahem, what I mean is, through a democratic process, more people from the larger factions······.”
Listening to them, I grew irritated and cut in.
“Did you gather here just to talk about this? I don't understand why you're selecting people in the first place. You could simply send everyone who wants to go.”
“That was our original intention, but the situation has changed somewhat.”
“Changed?”
Min Jiwon nodded.
“There's a limit on the number of people allocated to this scenario.”
······A limit?
“The dokkaebis should have sent the kings a separate message. It seems you haven't received yours yet.”
At that moment, a message appeared as though it had been waiting for its cue.
[The Seoul Dome's initial allocation is a total of 10 people.]
[Additional allocations will be determined by the deployed incarnations' progress in the scenario.]
Aha. So that was why they'd been arguing.
Unlike the other incarnations, who feared the scenarios, the ‘kings’ knew very well how important it was to gain an early foothold in one.
They probably thought that if they could deploy their own people in the initial allocation, control of the scenarios to come would pass to their group.
In the end, this gathering had been arranged for a game of musical chairs among the kings.
“My group will go. I've heard there are many Japanese people in that scenario area. So I believe it's only right that I, a descendant of Silla, take the lead.”
“No, I should go. Baekje had extensive exchanges with Japan from ancient times.”
“That was Baekje. Your sponsor is from Later Baekje.”
“What are you all talking about? Naturally, I should go. How can you put your faith in those outdated sponsors······?”
“Wait, everyone. Please calm down a little······.”
Jeon Ildo belatedly intervened, but the chaos showed no sign of being brought under control.
I sighed and looked to the side, meeting the King of Wanderers' eyes.
She had been watching me this whole time without saying a word.
Beneath her half-mask, I could see her mouth curved in a subtle smile.
Was she telling me to see if I could sort this out?
The emboldened kings radiated a savage air, as though they would balk even at bloodshed.
“There's no point in fighting among ourselves here.”
At those words, the kings turned toward me at once. Yoo Hyunho glared as though asking what I meant.
Feeling a faint vibration in the ground, I picked up a biscuit from the table.
So he'd finally arrived.
I'd been wondering what was taking him so long.
“Because the last ‘king’ hasn't arrived yet.”
The moment I bit into the biscuit, one side of the tent exploded, and the self-proclaimed President of Yeouido toppled forward with a scream.
“Aaaaargh!”
The figure of a man appeared, grinding his foot into the fallen Yoo Hyunho's back.
Through the tent he'd torn open, I could see dozens of sentries sprawled on the ground, spurting blood.
Just what I'd expect from our regressor.
No matter which round it was, that temper of his never changed.
His characteristically menacing gaze swept over the gathering, then fixed on me.
“The S-Supreme King······!”
Some of the kings turned deathly pale and groaned.
Then Yoo Joonghyuk, the Supreme King, spoke.
“I will announce the participants for the next scenario.”
As expected, there was no room for disagreement.
To him, selecting scenario participants was something to announce, not discuss.
“If you have any objections, I'll hear them now.”
How could anyone have an objection when he kept pouring out such terrifying killing intent?
Knowing Yoo Joonghyuk's overwhelming strength, the kings trembled, not even daring to consider resisting.
Ah, except for one person.
“M-Move! Get your foot off me!”
Unfortunately, His Excellency, the self-proclaimed President of Yeouido, apparently hadn't heard about the Supreme King. A politician, so out of touch with the rumors.
“Who the hell are you to suddenly show up and······!”
Crunch!
“Aaaaaaargh!”
Yoo Hyunho screamed as his hand was crushed.
“My hand! My hand!”
Crrrunch!
“Aaaaaaargh! Bodyguards! Where are my bodyguards?”

With his limbs crushed, Yoo Hyunho writhed and called for help, but there was no one here who could help him. Yoo Joonghyuk's foot pressed firmly into his back, and before long, Yoo Hyunho let out a strangled groan and passed out.
Once everything fell silent, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Apparently there are none. Then I'll announce the list.”
Tension spread across the kings' faces.
Yoo Joonghyuk really was impressive.
To tip the balance of power in his favor so easily······.
In an instant, the kings had been reduced from those ‘choosing’ to those ‘being chosen.’
I tore off a piece of jerky from the table and waited for Yoo Joonghyuk to speak.
Beside me, Min Jiwon, the King of Beauty, looked at me in disbelief.
「How can you be so calm?」
Sorry, but my situation was different from yours.
Because I was someone none other than Yoo Joonghyuk had acknowledged as a ‘companion.’
He might threaten me with talk of the oath being over and whatnot, but in the end, he'd acknowledged that he needed me.
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“The first is, of course, me.”
······Well, naturally.
Why would he leave himself off a list he'd made?
At some point, his companions had arrived behind him.
Lee Jihye and Lee Seolhwa.
I also saw Lee Hyunsung and Jung Heewon peering inside with worried eyes. Jung Heewon in particular looked ready to rush over at any moment, so I stopped her with a look.
Yoo Joonghyuk continued.
“The second is Lee Jihye.”
I'd assumed I would be second. That was unexpected.
Well, I hadn't been on his original list of companions, so the others might feel slighted if he picked me first.
He might seem cold, but he had a way of quietly looking after his own people.
I get how you feel, man.
Unable to hide her delight, Lee Jihye was looking at me with a broad grin.
······A little irritating.
“The third is Lee Seolhwa.”
Lee Seolhwa nodded and stepped forward.
With every name announced, the kings' faces grew darker.
They all sensed it.
That this list would become the final list.
「There are 7 slots left. We still have a chance.」
「The Supreme King's group consists of just those three, so he'll have to choose everyone else from outside his group.」
「At least we're the strongest of those remaining······.」
Their faces made it perfectly clear what they were thinking.
Me? Of course I wasn't worried.
Naturally, I'd be on the list.
Maybe the next name would finally be······.
“The fourth is Lee Hyunsung.”
Standing at the back, Lee Hyunsung turned pale when his name was suddenly called.
“M-Me, you mean······?”
Yoo Joonghyuk ignored the question and looked at the person beside Lee Hyunsung.
“The fifth is Jung Heewon.”
Startled, Jung Heewon opened her eyes wide.
Even I hadn't expected him to choose Jung Heewon.
Was this bastard just picking my companions now, too?
“The sixth is Lee Gilyoung.”
“······Huh? What?”
Then Yoo Joonghyuk looked at Shin Yoosung, who stood beside Lee Gilyoung.
Fear suddenly filled Shin Yoosung's eyes, and she hid behind Lee Gilyoung.

Flustered, Lee Gilyoung fidgeted briefly, then stepped in front of Shin Yoosung as though he'd made up his mind. Yoo Joonghyuk looked down at the two children with an inscrutable gaze, then turned his head.
At last, Yoo Joonghyuk's gaze landed on me.
Yes, finally, my turn.
So he'd deliberately saved me for last?
As expected of the protagonist. He knew how to stage a moment.
“······Decide the rest as you see fit.”
The whole piece of jerky went down at once, and I coughed.
Yoo Joonghyuk took one final look around the tent, gave me one final look as though I were pathetic, then turned and left as though he had no further business here.
What? That was it?
Really?
······Then what about me?
Why was he looking at me like that?
By the time I belatedly chased after him, Yoo Joonghyuk was already far out of sight.
How long had I stood there like that?

I patted Shin Yoosung's back and surveyed our surroundings. My head was in a muddle, but I couldn't remain like that.
Whether I looked ahead, whether I looked to the side, whether I looked behind. All I could see was forest.
Apparently, we'd landed right in the middle of a forested area.
For a scene in another world, it looked far too much like ‘Earth.’
[Main scenario ― ‘The Abandoned World’ has begun.]
The scenario message appearing immediately.
But I didn't have time to check the main scenario's details.
Because I could already sense movement in the nearby undergrowth.
“Yoosung.”
Having regained her senses, Shin Yoosung raised her head and steadied her breathing.
Rustling came from several places in the undergrowth.
One of the places where new scenario participants were warped in.
In the worst case, whatever was hiding in those bushes would be incarnations from other countries who'd arrived ahead of us.
Tensing, I readied myself to activate [Bookmark].
Those who'd warped into this world: probably the elite of the elite.
If I didn't give it my all from the start, I could lose my head in the blink of an eye.
But what emerged from the bushes was different from what we'd expected.
[Grade-7 monster species, ‘Steel Wolf,’ has appeared!]
At the words ‘grade-7 monster species,’ the same expression crossed both my face and Shin Yoosung's.
It was laughable.
We were probably the only ones who'd feel relieved by that message.
“They seem a little small, ajusshi.”
Considering that higher-grade monsters were usually the size of houses, the Steel Wolves that had just appeared were only the size of ordinary wolves.
Roughly ten to fifteen of them.
That wasn't a difficult number to deal with, either.
[Character ‘Shin Yoosung’ activates ‘Advanced Diverse Communication Lv.3’!]
Shin Yoosung used [Advanced Diverse Communication] to make the monsters kill one another, one by one.
I personally activated ‘Blade of Faith’ to finish off the ones Shin Yoosung couldn't tame.
They were unbelievably weak for grade-7 monsters.
It seemed their strength had diminished along with their size.
“······Huh? They're not giving us coins?”
“That event's over.”
“They're not giving us items, either. There aren't any cores.”
“That's because there's such a big gap between their stats and ours.”
“Are they really grade 7? They seem more like grade 9 to me······.”
Perhaps because she'd been so tense, only to find the first monsters we encountered so weak, Shin Yoosung looked a little deflated.
Come to think of it, something about the forest was a little strange.
Trees forming a forest like this should have towered far above my head, but even the tall trees here were only a little taller than me.
The scenario details were still unchanged, too.
Only the scenario title, ‘The Abandoned World,’ had appeared. Most of the fields were still filled with question marks.
[The conditions for scenario activation have not been met.]
I made a small jump to survey the surroundings.
Fortunately, the trees were short enough that a light jump was all it took to see the entire surrounding landscape.
“It's not all forest. Let's head out that way.”
In fact, I knew what would be waiting when we left this area.
We ran along a side path through the forest. Before long, the forest ended and wide-open plains appeared.
And there, on those plains.
“······Ajusshi?”
We encountered a body of troops.
“They've appeared! It's just as the scenario said!”
Someone shouted those words at us.
Although it must have been an alien language, it sounded like Korean.
Startled, Shin Yoosung faltered and backed toward me.
Troops that must have numbered at least several hundred filled part of the vast plain.
Dozens of cavalry and hundreds of archers.
And hundreds of infantry as well.
Enough people to wage a war had gathered there, waiting for us to emerge.
“Everyone, ready your skills!”
“Prepare to advance!”
Countless people radiated murderous intent as they leveled their spears and lances at us.
We hadn't done anything wrong, yet somehow we'd become the enemy.
“Attack―!”
Normally, the sight would certainly have been more than enough to overwhelm me.
If not for their size, that is.
“Waaaaah!”
Every one of the troops charging toward us across the plain was a little person (小人) about as tall as my fist.
“The people are so tiny!”
“They must be the inhabitants here.”
“We don't have to fight them, do we? We don't, right?”
Shin Yoosung spoke as she gradually backed away from the charging little people.
“······They're so small. I feel sorry for them.”
[You have encountered beings from another world. Check the scenario details.]
That was when screams rang out some distance away.
“D-disasters have appeared over there, too!”
“Aaaaaaagh!”
“Everyone, everyone, run! All troops, retreat!”
The little people charging at us suddenly pulled back their lines and began to flee.
In the distance, I could see incarnations indiscriminately trampling the little people to death.
“Hahahaha!”
“What's this? What an easy scenario!”
I couldn't hear them clearly, but it sounded like a foreign language being interpreted.
Two samurai wielding long swords.
They were Japanese.
As though they were playing a game, they drove their swords into the ground, slicing up the little people like insects.
Watching that scene of merciless slaughter, Shin Yoosung spoke in a horrified voice.
“······Ajusshi? What on earth is this scenario? What are we supposed to do?”
I knew why Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't wanted to bring Shin Yoosung.
Come to think of it, perhaps he was more humane than I was.
“Earth isn't the only place undergoing scenarios in the <Star Stream>.”
I pointed at the little people fleeing across the plain and said,
“And this is a scenario we're sharing with them.”
[A considerable number of constellations are hungry for blood and violence.]
[A considerable number of constellations are urging you to make a bold choice.]
[The main scenario is activating.]
<Main Scenario # 6 ― The Abandoned World>
Category : Main
Difficulty : S
Clear Conditions : Exterminate all dominant species on the planet ‘Peace Land’ in planetary system 9781.
Time Limit : 40 days
Reward : 200,000 coins, ???
Failure : ―
In the sixth scenario, our role was no longer to ‘stop the disasters.’
[You have become a ‘disaster’ for the planet ‘Peace Land.’]
Here, we had to become the disasters that would destroy this world.
